title: eSafety and Sport Integrity Australia Extend Online Abuse Partnership
body: eSafety Commissioner and Sport Integrity Australia have strengthened their partnership to better address online abuse in sport. The collaboration will focus on improving reporting mechanisms and support for athletes experiencing online harassment. Sporting clubs should ensure they have clear processes for responding to online abuse incidents.

title: Tennis Australia Strengthens Child Safety Screening Processes
body: Tennis Australia has implemented enhanced safeguarding measures to strengthen screening processes and prevent individuals with harmful histories from accessing children in tennis programs. The changes include improved Working With Children Check processes and additional vetting procedures for officials and volunteers.

title: Working with Children Check Reforms Delayed Nationally
body: A national database to support Working with Children Check reforms and continuous monitoring is still years away from being operational, despite being flagged as a top priority. The delay means states and territories continue to operate separate systems with known gaps that allow people with relevant offences to obtain clearances. Sporting clubs should remain vigilant with their own screening processes while waiting for system improvements.

title: NSW Reviewing Working with Children Check System
body: The NSW Government has opened public consultation on reforms to the Working with Children Check system, seeking input on strengthening child safety laws. This follows ongoing criticism of loopholes that allow people with certain criminal histories to work with children. Sporting organisations and clubs can contribute to the review to help shape future requirements.

title: Victoria Passes New Childcare Safety Protections
body: The Victorian Parliament has passed legislation strengthening safety protections in childcare settings following a rapid review that identified serious gaps. While focused on early childhood education, the reforms may signal broader changes to Working with Children Check requirements that could affect sporting clubs. Victorian clubs should monitor for any flow-on changes to their compliance obligations.

title: Victoria: Child Safety Reforms Strengthen Safeguards
body: New child safety laws have taken effect in Victoria, strengthening safeguards for children and young people across the state. The reforms build on existing Child Safe Standards requirements and introduce additional protections for organisations working with children. Clubs and sporting organisations should review their current policies to ensure compliance with the updated framework.

title: Victoria: Updated Guidance on Mandatory Reporting Obligations
body: The Victorian Government has released updated guidance on mandatory reporting and other child protection obligations for organisations. The resource clarifies who must report, what circumstances trigger reporting duties, and how to make a report to authorities. All sporting clubs in Victoria should ensure volunteers and staff understand these legal requirements.

title: Victoria: Child Safety Training and Resources Available
body: The Victorian Government has made child safety training and resources available to support organisations in meeting their obligations under the Child Safe Standards. The materials include guidance on creating child safe policies, implementing codes of conduct, and building child safe cultures. Clubs can access these free resources to strengthen their safeguarding practices.

title: Research: Community Sport Volunteers Need Better Child Safety Support
body: New research published in The Conversation has found that community sport volunteers need better support to keep children safe from abuse. The study highlights gaps in training, resources and organisational support for volunteers managing child safety responsibilities. The findings reinforce the importance of providing accessible guidance and practical tools to volunteer-run clubs.

title: Basketball Australia: New Child Safety Resources Launched
body: Basketball Australia has launched new child safety resources to strengthen its safe sport commitment across the basketball community. The resources are designed to help clubs and associations implement child safe practices and meet their obligations under national child safety frameworks. Basketball clubs should review these materials to support their safeguarding efforts.

title: WA Football: Integrity Unit Supports Child Safety
body: WA Football's Integrity Unit provides support and guidance to clubs on child safety and safeguarding matters across Western Australia. The unit handles child safety concerns, oversees compliance with child safe standards, and offers resources to help clubs create safe environments. WA football clubs can contact the Integrity Unit for advice on their child safety obligations.

title: Motorsport Australia: Child Safeguarding Integrity Framework
body: Motorsport Australia has established a safeguarding framework to protect children and young people participating in motorsport activities. The integrity program includes child safe policies, codes of conduct, and reporting mechanisms for concerns about child safety. All motorsport clubs and officials should familiarise themselves with these safeguarding requirements.

title: Queensland Rugby League: Child Safeguarding Partnership with SCS
body: The Queensland Rugby League is partnering with Safeguarding Children in Sport (SCS) to support child safeguarding practices across rugby league in Queensland. The partnership will help clubs access resources, training and guidance to create safer environments for children. QRL clubs are encouraged to engage with these safeguarding support services.

title: Working With Children Checks Not Reviewed After Sexual Misconduct Findings
body: An ABC investigation has revealed that Working With Children Checks are not being automatically reviewed when sexual misconduct findings are made against individuals in some Australian jurisdictions. This highlights significant gaps in how information is shared between agencies and raises concerns about the effectiveness of current screening systems. Sporting clubs should remain vigilant and report any concerns about volunteers or staff directly to their state's WWCC screening unit.

title: Volunteers Need Better Training to Handle Child Abuse Disclosures in Community Sport
body: New research from Victoria University confirms that community sport volunteers need more training and support to properly respond when children disclose abuse. The study found many volunteers feel unprepared to handle these situations and are unsure of their reporting obligations. Sporting clubs should ensure all volunteers understand mandatory reporting requirements and know how to respond appropriately to disclosures.

title: 543 Blue Cards Suspended Under New Queensland Powers
body: Queensland's Blue Card Services has suspended 543 working with children cards since March 2026 under new emergency suspension powers. The suspensions cover workers in childcare, sports clubs, and disability care settings who posed potential risks to children. Sporting clubs should ensure all volunteers and staff maintain current Blue Card status and understand their obligation to notify Blue Card Services of any changes in circumstances.

title: Queensland to Establish New Child Protection Commission
body: The Queensland Attorney-General has announced plans for a new child protection commission that will absorb existing Blue Card Services functions. The reform follows systemic reviews into child safeguarding failures across sectors including sport. Sporting clubs should monitor announcements for any changes to Blue Card processes or requirements as the new commission is established.

title: Multiple Blue Card System Failures Exposed in Queensland Cases
body: Recent cases in Queensland have revealed significant gaps in the Blue Card screening system, with offenders maintaining working with children clearances despite serious charges. Reviews highlight failures in information sharing between agencies and delays in suspension processes. Sporting clubs must remain vigilant with their own safeguarding practices and not rely solely on Blue Card checks as their only child safety measure.

title: eSafety Commissioner releases new research on cyberbullying in children's sport
body: The eSafety Commissioner has published research titled 'The digital sideline: Exploring cyberbullying and online hate by people connected to children's sports'. The study examines online abuse directed at young athletes and provides insights for sporting organisations. This research complements existing eSafety resources for sports administrators, coaches, parents and young athletes.

title: National sporting bodies commit to tackling online harm
body: National sporting leaders have joined forces with the eSafety Commissioner to address online abuse and harassment in Australian sport. The partnership aims to strengthen protections for athletes, officials and participants across all levels of sport. Sporting organisations should review their existing online safety policies and consider how they align with the eSafety Commissioner's guidance.

title: eSafety Commissioner releases guide for sport organisations on social media age restrictions
body: The eSafety Commissioner has published new guidance to help sporting organisations understand their responsibilities under social media age restriction laws. The resource explains what the changes mean for clubs managing youth programs and communicating with junior members online. Sporting organisations should review their social media policies and practices in light of the new requirements.

title: New online safety codes introduce protections for children
body: The eSafety Commissioner has introduced new online safety codes that provide enhanced protections for children using digital platforms. These codes may affect how sporting clubs operate online programs and communicate with junior participants. Clubs should familiarise themselves with the new requirements to ensure their digital practices remain compliant.

title: Updated parental controls guidance for keeping children safe online
body: The eSafety Commissioner has released updated guidance on parental controls to help families keep children safe online. Sporting clubs working with junior members may find this resource useful when advising parents about online safety in sport contexts. The guidance covers practical steps for managing children's digital safety across devices and platforms.

title: eSafety Commissioner launches campaign on online abuse in sport
body: The eSafety Commissioner has published new guidance specifically addressing online abuse in sporting contexts. The resource provides practical advice for sporting clubs and participants on preventing and responding to online harassment and abuse. This builds on eSafety's existing partnership work with Sport Integrity Australia.
